### Observed differences

- In the earlier window every trace ran the same single-pass chain: A02, then A04, then A03, each exactly once per trace, with A02 always followed by A04 and A04 always followed by A03. [OCC001, DIR001, DIR002]
- In the later window A02 repeats: it occurs about 2.1 times per trace on average, with at least one repeat in about 50 in 100 traces, whereas before it occurred exactly once in every trace and never repeated. [OCC001]
- In the later window A02's exits split: about 53 in 100 of its outgoing transitions still go to A04, but about 47 in 100 now go directly to A03, a transition not observed before. [DIR001]
- In the later window A04's successor flipped completely: before it always led to A03, now it always leads back to A02, producing an A02–A04 back-and-forth. [DIR002]
- In the later window A04 appears in only about 99 of 200 traces (before: all 200); where A02 and A04 still occur together, they interleave or repeat in every such case instead of running once in a fixed order. [POS002, REL002]
- The fixed ordering loosened: A02 precedes A03 in only about 50 in 100 later traces (before: always), with the rest interleaved or repeated; A03 precedes A04 in about 22 in 100 traces where both occur (before: A04 always preceded A03), with about 28 in 100 interleaved. [REL001, REL003]
- Distances changed accordingly: A02→A03 was always two steps apart and is now one step in about 40 in 100 of the observed cases (three or five steps in most of the rest); A04→A03 was always adjacent and is now typically two or four steps apart; immediate A02→A04 successions fell from all cases to about 18 in 100. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
- Relative positions shifted consistently with this: A02's typical position moved later (median about 0.5 to about 0.67, with new spread) and A04's mean position moved earlier (about 0.75 to about 0.56). [POS001, POS002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural reorganisation of the control flow around A02, A03 and A04 as a possibility. In the earlier window each trace executed one pass of A02 → A04 → A03; in the later window A02 runs about 2.1 times per trace with repeats in about half the traces, A04 — when present — always returns to A02 so that A02 and A04 form a repeating cycle, A02 can close directly to A03 (about 47 in 100 of its exits), and A04 is not observed at all in about half the traces. The successor changes at A02 and A04 and the repetition of A02 are observed directly, and the relation, distance and position items all agree with this same picture. Screening found 11 qualifying control-flow items in a family where about 0.06 would be expected if nothing had changed, so sampling variation alone cannot account for the ensemble. [OCC001, DIR001, DIR002, REL001, REL002, REL003, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, POS002]

Limitations: the items draw on the same traces, so they corroborate one underlying difference rather than providing independent confirmations. The data cannot distinguish a strictly sequential loop from interleaved or concurrent repetitions of A02 and A04, and they cannot show why A04 is missing in about half of the later traces — only that it was not observed there. [REL002, REL003, POS002]
